name: FFmpeg
description: Audio and video conversion through the bundled ffmpeg executable.

sharedOptions.label: Extra arguments
sharedOptions.description: Appended verbatim before the output file. For anything the options above do not cover.

argumentSuffix.comment: Empty when the option is blank, so nothing is added.

targets.label: MP3
targets.description: MPEG layer 3 through libmp3lame.

targets.label: FLAC
targets.description: Lossless.

options.label: Compression level
options.description: Higher is smaller and slower. Never affects quality.

options.label: Quality
options.description: -1 is smallest, 10 is best. 5 is roughly 160 kbit/s.

options.label: Quality (CRF)
options.description: Lower is better. 18 is visually lossless, 28 is small.

options.label: Encoder speed
options.description: Slower presets give smaller files at the same quality.

arguments.comment: Lets Apple players open HEVC in MP4.
Required for CRF mode with these encoders.

options.label: Quality (CRF)
options.description: Lower is better. 31 is a good VP9 default.

arguments.comment: A GIF or PNG source decodes with an alpha channel, which VP9 and AV1 refuse.

targets.label: GIF (from video)
targets.description: Two-pass palette generation for a GIF that does not look like 1998.

arguments.comment: An output rate rather than an fps filter, so a single frame input is held rather than dropped.

targets.label: WMA
targets.description: Windows Media Audio, for players that accept nothing newer.

targets.label: AC-3
targets.description: Dolby Digital, the surround format home cinema receivers expect.

targets.label: AIFF
targets.description: Uncompressed, the way WAV is, but at home on a Mac.

targets.label: ALAC (Apple Lossless)
targets.description: Lossless in a container iTunes and iOS will open.

targets.label: Matroska audio (MKA)
targets.description: Holds any audio codec, including several tracks at once.

targets.label: QuickTime (MOV)
targets.description: Including ProRes, which is what editing software wants as an intermediate.

targets.label: Ogg Theora
targets.description: Patent-free video for anywhere WebM is not an option.

targets.label: MPEG-2
targets.description: What DVD authoring tools and older set-top boxes read.

targets.label: MPEG transport stream (TS)
targets.description: Streamable and safe to cut anywhere, which is why broadcast uses it.

targets.label: Animated WebP
targets.description: A GIF replacement at a fraction of the size, with all its colours.

targets.label: PNG (single frame)
targets.description: Grabs one frame, for a thumbnail or a poster image.

options.label: Position
options.description: Where to take the frame, as hh:mm:ss.

arguments.comment: Placed after -i so the seek is exact rather than fast.

targets.label: Animated PNG
targets.description: An animated GIF without the 256 colour limit, and with real transparency.

targets.label: MP4 (H.265, smaller)

options.label: Quality (CRF)
options.description: Lower is better. 18 is visually lossless, 28 is small.

options.label: Encoder speed
options.description: Slower presets give smaller files at the same quality.

arguments.comment: Lets Apple players open HEVC in MP4.

targets.description: About half the size of H.264 at the same quality. Plays on anything recent.

targets.label: MP4 (AV1, smallest)

options.label: Quality (CRF)
options.description: Lower is better. 18 is visually lossless, 28 is small.

arguments.comment: Preset 8 is the usual balance of speed and size for SVT-AV1.

targets.description: The most efficient codec here, and the slowest to encode. Needs a player from the last few years.

options.label: Quality (CRF)
options.description: Lower is better. 18 is visually lossless, 28 is small.

options.label: Encoder speed
options.description: Slower presets give smaller files at the same quality.

arguments.comment: Lets Apple players open HEVC in MP4.

targets.label: MP4 without sound
targets.description: The same picture with the audio track removed.

options.label: Re-encode the picture
options.description: Off copies the picture untouched, which is instant but only works when it is already H.264 or H.265.

targets.label: ProRes (MOV, for editing)
targets.description: Large files that every editing program scrubs through smoothly.

arguments.comment: H.263 only takes a handful of fixed sizes, so the picture is fitted into CIF.

targets.label: JPEG (single frame)
targets.description: Grabs one frame as a JPEG, smaller than the PNG.

options.label: Position
options.description: Where to take the frame, as hh:mm:ss.

arguments.comment: Placed after -i so the seek is exact rather than fast.

targets.label: iPhone ringtone (M4R)
targets.description: AAC in the container an iPhone takes as a ringtone, cut to length.

options.label: Length
options.description: iOS refuses ringtones longer than 40 seconds.

targets.label: AMR (voice)
targets.description: The phone voice codec: tiny, mono and meant for speech.

targets.label: Audio track, untouched (MKA)
targets.description: Takes the sound out of a video exactly as it is, without re-encoding. Instant and lossless.
